title: Why Do SwiftUI Apps “Stutter”?
partialText: SwiftUI is a powerful tool that tracks every dependency in your UI and updates exactly what needs updating. The Attribute Graph is a directed acyclic graph (DAG) that SwiftUI constructs from your view hierarchy. A dependency is recorded **at the moment of access, not at the point of declaration.

title: Why Water Became Our Universal Reference (and Why O Coins Use It)
partialText: After the French Revolution, the new metric system tied the kilogram to water: originally, the mass of one liter of water under carefully defined conditions. That was not random. Water is everywhere humans live, the common denominator of life on Earth, and the one thing we all need regardless of culture, diet, or climate. Some drink wine, others tea; some eat rice, others potatoes—but everyone needs water. For any universal measurement, the reference must be observable and comparable for all. That is why, at O International, we calibrate the value of our digital currencies using the local price of water in each national currency: the same logic that made water the ancestor of the kilogram now anchors a stable, global monetary system.

title: Why Beautiful Apps Die Lonely Deaths: The Structural Forces Behind Vibe Decay
partialText: The AI vibe decay problem is not a new phenomenon, but AI tooling has supercharged it. The marginal cost of producing a polished interface, a compelling demo, and a well-written landing page has collapsed. The marginal cost of building something people actually want, use, and return to has not. So we have a glut of beautiful apps with no users.

title: Why "100% Test Coverage" Is a Vanity Metric
partialText: 100% test coverage feels great on a slide deck. It means almost nothing in production. Teams that fixate on coverage numbers end up writing low-value tests that pad the metric while real bugs slip through. The smarter move: measure what your tests actually catch, not how many lines they touch.

title: Fighting VRAM Overheating: 3 Unexpected Lessons from My First Windows Utility
partialText: My RTX 4080 laptop was thermal throttling during Stable Diffusion renders because the VRAM Memory Junction hit 105°C. Standard undervolting wasn't enough. I built a Windows utility (VRAM Shield) using "Pulse Throttling" to micro-suspend processes and manage thermals dynamically. Here are the 3 biggest lessons I learned about hardware management.

title: Kafka Has Become the Postgres of Streaming — And That Changes Everything
partialText: Kafka has crossed the commodity threshold — reliable, ubiquitous, and no longer a strategic differentiator. Like Postgres before it, Kafka's success is also its ceiling for vendors trying to build businesses on it. The hard problems have moved up the stack: lakehouse integration, cost efficiency, governance, and real-time context for AI. Commoditization isn't failure. It's the foundation everything else gets built on.

title: The "No-Code" Scaling Paradox: Why Your Frankenstein Architecture Will Eventually Fail
